post-brief.response: No, it is unsafe because the same-value `Release` RMW forces an order in the parent's modification order against the collector's `Acquire` clear—either landing after the clear to re-set the parent bit, or landing before it to synchronize-with the clear so the leaf write happens-before the collector's leaf visit—whereas a `Relaxed` load neither writes to the parent nor establishes a release-acquire edge. Counterexample: with leaf bit `L1` and parent bit `P` previously set by `W1`, writer `W2` sets leaf bit `L2` and returns early after its `Relaxed` load of `P` still reads `W1`'s pre-clear `1`, while the collector clears `P` with an `Acquire` RMW (synchronizing only with `W1`), visits the leaf observing only `L1` (missing `L2` because there is no happens-before edge from `W2` to the collector), drains `L1` without rearming `P`, and leaves `L2` stranded beneath an empty root that falsely passes closure under the exclusive mark gate.
